title.narrative: Skills for Industry Competitiveness and Innovation Program

description.narrative: The results-based program (RBL) will increase the provision of skilled workforce for industry competitiveness and innovation. The program will have the following outputs: (i) training for advanced technical skills in priority and emerging sectors improved, (ii) managerial capabilities and green innovation capacity strengthened, (iii) socially inclusive skilling and upskilling expanded, and (iv) institutional capacity for skills monitoring and management enhanced.

Output: Capacity for advanced technical skills training developed for emerging and priority sectors Indicator: At least 20 advanced technical courses implemented based on industry demands, including at least 3 courses specifically targeted for women (2023 baseline: Not applicable) (OP 3.2.2) Progress/Status: 7 new advanced courses on light engineering have commenced in BITAC. 7 advanced-level courses on fashion and garments have started at BUFT, ILET (5 courses), BRAC-IT (8 courses) & BRAC-Pharma (1 course) have been signed for 31 advanced courses of which 15 have already started. The rest are going to start soon. Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

Output: Capacity for advanced technical skills training developed for emerging and priority sectors Indicator: At least 3 international partnerships established for advanced technical courses (2023 baseline: Not applicable) (OP 7.3.3) Progress/Status: 3 MOUs for advanced training in the textile, automotive and light engineering sectors have been signed till date, as follows: (i) MOU among SICIP, MOTJ, and KOTERI; (ii) MOU among SICIP, DTE, and HRI; (iii) MOU among SICIP, BITAC and KoreaTech
Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

Output: Capacity for advanced technical skills training developed for emerging and priority sectors Indicator: At least 35 practical training labs or workshops in advanced technologies created and operational for training (e.g., BUFT, STTLs, BITAC, polytechnics), including green technologies (2023 baseline: Not applicable) (DLI 4) (OP 3.1.3; 3.2.5) Progress/Status: 6 practical training labs for advanced light engineering in BITAC are already operational. Construction of STTL lab in Chittagong textile engineering college has begun. Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

Output: Capacity for advanced technical skills training developed for emerging and priority sectors Indicator: At least 4,800 people (at least 15% women) enrolled in industry-demanded advanced or emerging technology courses (2023 baseline: Not applicable) (DLI 3) (OP 1.1.1; 2.1.1; 2.2.1) Progress/Status: 461 trainees (48 female) have enrolled in advanced technical courses on light engineering and fashion and garments Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

Output: Access to socially inclusive skilling and upskilling expanded Indicator: At least 18,000 people enrolled in international certificate courses for potential migrant workers (2023 baseline: 5 courses under SEIP) (DLI 8) (OP 1.1.1) Progress/Status: 152 people (12 female) have commenced internationally certified training at Asia Technical Training Institute for TÜV SÜD certification and at BMET for City & Guilds certification.
Contracts for additional courses with certification by Bureau Veritas (with AEOSIB and BEIOA) , TAKAMOL SVP of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and City and Guilds (with BMET) are under preparation.
Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

As of 30 Sep 2025, 291 job placement has done, out of them 58 were women from REHAB and LFMEAB. Data Source: Semiannual progress reports, TMS reports Actual value:

As of 31 Dec 2025, a.2,197 trainees have completed training on sector-relevant technical and managerial skills, out of which 658 are female (30%).
